name: Alexamorelin

lead: Alexamorelin is a lab-made peptide related to hexarelin that stimulates growth hormone release. The draw is more growth hormone, which people link to muscle gain and fat loss.

As a growth hormone secretagogue, it is described as raising the body's own GH output rather than supplying GH itself. A 2000 study reported its endocrine effects in humans. It appears in the literature mainly as one of the peptides that anti-doping laboratories screen for; no study has tested it for muscle or appearance outcomes.

paras: It is rare and obscure, appearing mostly in lists of GH secretagogues. There is no established routine for it.
No clinical-trial safety data were found. It is not an approved drug and is covered by sports drug-testing screens.

angle.text: Alexamorelin is a hexarelin-related peptide listed among growth hormone secretagogues, where the appeal is more GH for muscle and fat loss. A 2000 study reported its hormonal effects in humans.

lead: Alexamorelin is a synthetic heptapeptide growth hormone secretagogue, related to hexarelin, with the sequence Ala-His-D-2-methyl-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2. A 2000 study reported its endocrine activities in humans [1].

It has not been approved as a medicine. It appears in the scientific literature mainly as one of the growth hormone releasing peptides (GHRPs) that anti-doping laboratories screen for in urine [2][3][4]. It is named among the prohibited peptides covered by sports drug-testing methods [3][4].
No published trials have tested it for any appearance or muscle-related outcome.
infobox: Included in peptide screening panels for sports drug testing [3][4]

paras: The only identified human study is a 2000 report of its endocrine activities as a synthetic GH secretagogue [1]. No trials of muscle, body-composition or cosmetic outcomes were found.

Alexamorelin is listed among growth hormone releasing peptides for which urine screening assays have been developed, because such orally active peptides can raise endogenous GH while escaping the standard test for exogenous GH [2][3]. Mass-spectrometry methods for these peptides have been refined repeatedly [5][4][6].

A 2025 study used human hepatocyte incubations to identify metabolites that could serve as markers of alexamorelin consumption [7]. A 2026 workflow paper includes peptidic doping agents in blood matrices [8].

timeline.event: Alexamorelin included in peptide doping-screening methods [2][3][4].
Metabolite markers of consumption identified in vitro [7].
